transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm explaining this the right way, but I'm here because... well, I've been having a bit of a hard time focusing. I keep getting hit, just sort of out of nowhere, with the scene of my cousin on that pavement. 

It's probably just stress, but it feels so real. Like I can hear the shouting and see the lights all over again, even when I'm just standing in the church office trying to act normal and do my job. It's a little embarrassing, honestly, to lose my composure like that. I'm sorry, does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me more about these moments when you see your cousin on the pavement again? Do these experiences feel like memories that keep coming back to you, even when you don’t want them to?

Yes, exactly. Um, sorry if I'm just repeating what I said a second ago, I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. But yes, they... they definitely come back when I really, really don't want them to. 

Like I mentioned, I'll just be standing there in the church office, trying to act completely normal and do my job, and then it just forces its way into my head. The whole scene of my cousin on the pavement. It's so vivid that I can hear all the shouting and see the flashing lights all over again. I really try to push it down and ignore it because I know I need to keep it together and be a good example for my parishioners, but... it just hits me out of nowhere. I'm trying my best to handle it, I really am. Am I explaining that okay? Is that the kind of detail you were looking for?
